In [[graph theory]], the '''Goldberg–Seymour conjecture''' states that, for a [[multigraph]] <math>G</math><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://faculty.math.illinois.edu/~west/openp/|title=Problems in Graph Theory and Combinatorics|website=faculty.math.illinois.edu|access-date=2019-05-05}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |first=Guangming |last=Jing |title=The Goldberg-Seymour Conjecture on the edge coloring of multigraphs |date=2018 |publisher=Georgia State University |url=https://math.gsu.edu/gchen/files/PPT/Guangming_ALS.pdf}}</ref>

: <math>\operatorname{\chi'}(G) \leq \max(1 + \operatorname{\Delta}(G),\, \operatorname{\Gamma}(G))</math>

where <math>\operatorname{\chi'}(G)</math> is the [[edge coloring|edge chromatic number]] of ''G'', <math>\operatorname{\Delta}(G)</math> is its maximum [[degree (graph theory)|degree]], and

: <math>\operatorname{\Gamma} G = \max_{H \subset G} \frac{|E(H)|}{\lfloor\frac{1}{2} |V(H)| \rfloor}.</math>

This above quantity is twice the [[arboricity]] of&nbsp;''G''. It is sometimes called the '''density''' of&nbsp;''G''.<ref name=":1" />

Here, ''G'' can be a [[multigraph]] and can have [[loop (graph theory)|loop]]s. For simple graphs, this result follows from [[Vizing's theorem]].

== Background ==
It is already known that for [[simple graph|loopless]] ''G'' (but can have parallel edges):<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />

: <math>\operatorname{\chi'} G \geq \max(\operatorname{\Delta} G, \lceil \operatorname{\Gamma} G \rceil).</math>

When does equality not hold? It does not hold for the [[Petersen graph]]. It is hard to find other examples. It is currently unknown whether there are any [[planar graph]]s for which equality does not hold.

This [[conjecture]] is named after Mark K. Goldberg of [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Goldberg|first=Mark|date=1984|title=Edge-coloring of multigraphs: Recoloring technique|journal=[[Journal of Graph Theory]]|volume=8|issue=1|pages=123–137|doi=10.1002/jgt.3190080115}}</ref> and [[Paul Seymour (mathematician)|Paul Seymour]] of [[Princeton University]], who arrived to it independently of Goldberg.<ref name=":0" />

== Announced proof ==
In 2019, an alleged [[mathematical proof|proof]] was announced by Chen, Jing, and Zang in the paper.<ref name=":0">{{Cite arXiv|last1=Zang|first1=Wenan|last2=Jing|first2=Guangming|last3=Chen|first3=Guantao|date=2019-01-29|title=Proof of the Goldberg–Seymour Conjecture on Edge-Colorings of Multigraphs|class=math.CO|language=en|eprint=1901.10316v1}}</ref> Part of their proof was to find a suitable generalization of [[Vizing's theorem]] (which says that for simple graphs <math>\operatorname{\chi'} G \leq 1 + \operatorname{\Delta} G</math>) to multigraphs. In 2023, Jing<ref name=":4">{{cite arXiv|last=Jing|first=Guangming|date=2023-08-29|title=On Edge Coloring of Multigraphs|eprint=2308.15588|class=math.CT}}</ref>
announced a new proof with a [[polynomial-time]] edge coloring algorithm achieving the conjectured [[upper and lower bounds|bound]].
